name: Name
title: DEAD ON\nARRIVAL
body: By Matthew D. Wilson

name: Name
body:
The impenetrable walls of Caspia loomed before the baron and his two henchmen as their weary horses cantered toward the northern gate. Unlike every other time Baron Caldwell had visited Caspia, the ocean-blue pennons emblazoned with Cygnar’s golden swan were nowhere to be seen. Instead, the ensigns that normally adorned the crown jewel of Cygnar had been replaced with solid black streamers and banners, crying out with their lack of extravagance that the nation was mourning its fallen king.
A chorus of bells rang out from within the city, nine chimes in all, audible even at a fair distance from the gate. Though his body ached after the long ride through the night, Caldwell was buoyant with self-satisfaction after reaching the city so early—until he spotted the dozens of carriages and hundreds of travelers awaiting entrance through the gate. He was expecting a queue, as anyone entering Caspia was subjected to a rigorous interrogation process to verify identity and the purpose of their visit, but the king’s pending funeral was drawing travelers from all over Cygnar, creating a backup that could take hours, hours Caldwell couldn’t afford if he were going to maintain his lead on Wolfe.

name: Name
body:
Hemmed in on both sides by a low stone wall and gutters, the final mile of the King’s Highway was easily large enough for a pair of wagons to comfortably pass each other with a third sitting in the middle, but the cobblestone road was now choked with carriages, horses, and travelers on foot, all conspiring to prevent the baron and his henchmen from an easy path forward. Jagged rocks beyond the road made bypassing the causeway treacherous on foot and impossible on horseback, so the only approach to the northern gate was the long avenue ahead. But despite his cordial requests of others to move out of the way and claims of official business and urgent matters of national security, the farther the baron pushed on, the more tightly packed the travelers became. And the tighter they were packed, the more restless and irritable they appeared until they eventually outright refused to allow him to pass.
"Who do you think you are, shoving through like that?" a burly farmer challenged, pushing up the sleeves of his tunic.

name: Name
body: "Get to the end of the line where you belong!" a woman shrieked, hanging out of the window of a carriage to make sure Caldwell wouldn’t miss her vulgar gesture. "Look here," the baron shouted over the rising din of impatient travelers, "there’s a threat coming, and I need to get word to the proper authorities. You’re all in danger." The farmer seized the bridle of Caldwell’s horse, brandishing his ham hock of a fist at the baron. "You push one step past me, and you’ll be the one in danger." Caldwell backed off and regrouped with his two henchmen. There were a hundred yards left to cover, but he’d never get past the logjam of lowborn cretins blocking it without risking a life-threatening confrontation. Walking his own horse between each of his bannermen, he motioned for them to lean in as he whispered. "Lads, I’m going to need you to create a distraction." Both of the henchmen gaped at Caldwell before the elder of the two finally spoke up. "They’ll eat us alive if we get bully, my lord."

name: Name
body:
"Better than being eaten alive by one of those Iosan demons on their way here," Caldwell spat. "And that’s exactly what you can look forward to if I don’t get through that gate."
Resigned to the pain they knew was coming, both men nodded.
A few moments later, the two coaxed their horses forward, slowly pushing aside those pedestrians wary enough of being trampled to yield to the horses that were becoming increasingly agitated by the cramped quarters. Soon, angry protests erupted from the crowd with all manner of colorful insults thrown at them followed quickly by rotten produce and whatever rocks could be scavenged. Still, the henchmen pushed forward until they could gain no more ground on horseback. Wrestling free of the throng of flailing arms attempting to pull them from their saddles, they clambered up to stand atop their horses then leaped the top of a nearby carriage.
Caldwell nodded as the two men glanced back at him, then watched smugly as the crowd swarmed around them while they scrambled from the roof of one carriage, across the backs of the horses yoked to it, onto the back of another carriage and so on, working their way toward the gate with arms raised to deflect the barrage of projectiles assailing them.

name: Name
body:
"Good lads. Loyal to the bone," he said under his breath as his bannermen drew the attention of every person within line of sight.
Dismounting, Caldwell abandoned his horse and weaved through the outraged horde drawn to the antics of his henchmen. More than once he deflected potential scrutiny by pointing and yelling, "Look at those two miscreants trying to shortcut the queue!" Within minutes, he had found the beginning of the line and slipped in front of a carriage while its coachman was distracted by the uproar behind him. And before the coachman could notice, Caldwell was the next to be called upon by the gate watchmen.
A small army of armored watchmen had been deployed to the northern gate and they were clearly overwhelmed by the endless mass of travelers seeking entrance to the city. They wore black sashes across their polished steel cuirasses and dour expressions as they struggled to admit the horde, one party at a time, in some semblance of order.
A weary gatekeeper with a crooked nose motioned Caldwell to step forward and rattled off the customary challenge for what was surely the hundredth time that morning. The bars on his collar identified him as a captain of the city watch.

name: Name
body: "State your name, your origin, and your business in Caspia." A young scribe stood just behind him, quill in hand, ready to record Caldwell’s declaration into a leather-bound ledger. With a flourish, the baron obliged. "I am Baron Abercrombie Caldwell, Lord Consul of the Cygnaran Duchy of the Eastern Midlunds. And I am here on a matter of grave importance bearing a message for the queen regent." At Caldwell’s reply, the watch captain perked up. Seemingly bemused, his eyes narrowed as he looked the baron up and down. "Well now, we’ve got a baron here, we do. Did you get that, Wembly? Did you get all that in the book, now? "Abercrombie Caldwell," the baron repeated for the benefit of the scribe, "Lord Consul of Cygnaran Duchy of —" "We got it, m’lord," the watchman cut him off. "Most of the barons coming through here ain’t so comfortable on their feet. Usually got some fancy hackney and a…what’dya call them folks that dotes on the hoity-toities, Wembly?" The scribe cleared his throat. "An entourage, sir."

name: Name
body: "An entourage." The watchman searched behind Caldwell. "Did you misplace your entourage, m’lord?" Caldwell resisted the impulse to assert his station. The watchman was already predisposed to deny ingress to anyone he had truck with, and he had the authority to do so. The baron needed a man on his side to get him inside. "My companions have been…delayed." He looked over his shoulder at the still broiling chaos his bannermen had incited, pausing to make sure it wasn’t about to spill over in the middle of his negotiation. "Delayed by this unruly mob that lacks the proper respect for your considerable efforts, my good man. But the message I bear is of the utmost importance and worth every inconvenience necessary to deliver it to the proper authority." "Note the entourage’s delay, Wembly," the watch captain said, starting to lose interest. "Best you return to them and enter together," He waved his hand to dismiss the baron entirely. "I cannot," Caldwell said, clasping his hands pleadingly before him. "There is a dire threat on its way to Caspia and I must warn the crown."

name: Name
body: He paused, lowering his voice and leaning in so only the watchman would be privy to the clandestine information he was about to disclose. "It’s the Iosans. Again." At this, the watchman raised an eyebrow. "You don’t say. My brother—a trencher, he was—lost his arm in a battle with those long-eared fanatics. Hating our kind, they do, and for nothing more than minding our own business." Nothing like a common enemy for finding common ground, thought Caldwell. "They’re even worse now. Cannibals, they’ve become. And they’ve bewitched an entire battalion of the Storm Legion who are leading them here as we speak." "Got a wire this morning that said we’d be receiving a Legion from King’s Vine today." "That’s the one." "Storm Legion." The watch captain sneered as he said the words. "All their fancy gear and those prissy bastards still can’t handle a few bush twigs?" "Have they ever even been in a real fight?" Caldwell said. The watchman clutched his belly as he laughed. "Har! Who’s got time to fight with all that shiny armor needin’ polishing?"

name: Name
body:
"You and I have a great deal in common. So, here’s the situation. I need an escort to Warmaster Ebonhart. I have to let him know of the treachery that has taken place before it can infiltrate the city."
"Look…Abercrombie…er, m’lord, if it’s as you’ve said it—" The watch captain’s demeanor had become genuinely concerned and sober. "—the king’s funeral is tomorrow. Every living soul in the city is preparing for the formalities. I’m sorry, truly I am, but you’re not going to get anywhere near the Warmaster today, not even his footman."
Caldwell grinned. He had overcome the barrier. Now it was just a matter of applying the proper incentive. "I understand the peril involved with getting me in front of someone  who can do something about the approaching threat."
He reached into his vest and produced a velvet pouch. Loosening the ties at the top, he exposed a fistful of golden crowns—easily a month’s wages for a watchman, probably more. "I’m willing to risk it if you are."
The captain’s eyes opened wide as he stared down at the purse full of coins. "For that, I could get you in front of the queen."

name: Name
body:
"Promise to stall those Legion prigs as long as possible, and it’s all yours," Caldwell said, offering the purse.
"Wembly," the captain said, transfixed with the gold in his hands, "note down the baron’s entrance has been approved."
***

name: Name
body:
Queen Marjorie sat at the head of the large oval table that dominated the circular hall of Cygnar’s Inner Council chamber. Suspended from the ceiling behind her was a massive golden Cygnus, the crest of Cygnar emblazoned upon a shield cast in three tons of iron.
She focused her eyes on the map of Immoren covering the table, inlaid with lines of gold and silver in the massive slab of varnished oak. It gave her a way to avoid eye contact with any of the six men who flanked her at the table, lest their attention be drawn from debating each other to confronting her directly on whatever detail they might be fixated on in the moment.
While she listened intently to the discourse between the high chancellors whose ultimate responsibility was to advise Cygnar’s crown on all matters of state, she was unable to keep her mind from drifting to the matters that weighed on her heart. She longed to be with her two young sons, to comfort them on the eve of their father’s funeral, and to grieve for the untimely passing of her husband. And yet she was the queen regent, appointed by Julius on his deathbed to govern the great kingdom of Cygnar in his absence until young Woldred was of age and experience enough to assume the throne. For five days now, she had been Cygnar’s highest power. Were she to defer to this council of graying old men now, if she failed to assert her voice whether from weakness or despair, she knew she would be forfeiting her hand in the governance of Cygnar’s future.

name: Name
body:
The matter currently derailing a more appropriate observation of family affairs was the untimely wire received from Point Bourne earlier in the day. The six old men around her were helpless in the grip of its allegations and implications.
"It’s absolutely preposterous." Warmaster General Kielon Ebonhart IV, on Marjorie’s left, pounded the table with a heavy fist, his white-bearded jaw quivering with his conviction. "Who would believe such nonsense?"
On Marjorie’s right, the Lord High Chancellor Leto Raelthorne, who had once ruled Cygnar before Julius had taken the throne, responded in a carefully measured tone. "But what if it is true? What if, after all this time, they have returned?"
"From the Bay of Stone to the Gulf of Cygnar, our shores are secure. If the Orgoth have made the mistake of returning to Immoren, they will not land on Cygnaran soil." Marjorie’s great uncle, the heavyset Navarch Galten Sparholm III, seemed sleepy in his response, perhaps too comfortable in Cygnar’s continued naval domination over the seas of the Meredius.

name: Name
body: Scout General Bolden Rebald smoothed his thin black mustache with a gloved finger and thumb and read the wire aloud once again. "Orgoth have attacked. Marching on Khardov. Send reinforcements with Dusk posthaste. Iron Kingdoms must not fall." He scoffed. "Looks authentic. But Khador hasn’t referred to themselves as being part of the Iron Kingdoms since the Corvis Treaties, at least not in formal terms. The reference here smacks of misdirection. Whoever sent this is playing at something." "How can you be sure?" asked Polk, the Lord of Industry for all of Cygnar. "If any bit of this is true, it will be a significant disruption to our foreign trade." "We can worry about trade later," said Ebonhart. "If any of this is true, we could be headed for all-out war." Rebald narrowed his eyes and stroked his chin. "All-out war with whom? The ancient boogeymen in our history books? Or could this be some sort of ploy to get us to commit our resources and attention to the north while leaving us vulnerable elsewhere? We haven’t heard from Cryx in quite a while."

name: Name
body: "Isn’t it your job to bring us that intelligence, spymaster?" Polk said. "I know for certain that you haven’t brought anything to the table resembling intelligence," Rebald replied with a sneer. Unsurprisingly, Lord Treasurer Lars Corumny interjected his typically conservative stance. "We should await approving any expenditures until we understand the full scope of the situation." Sighing, Marjorie shoved aside her more persistent thoughts and gazed at each of the lord chancellors. The youngest of them was over twice her age, yet for all their experience and wisdom, they seemed more likely to debate the subject endlessly than arrive at any plan of action. Clearing her throat loudly to get their attention, she asked, "What is the Dusk?" There was a long pause as each of the chancellors cast their eyes around the table looking for someone who might have an answer. "The wire says, ‘send reinforcements with Dusk’," Marjorie said, in case the chancellors didn’t understand what she was referencing. "What does that mean?"

name: Name
body:
Sparholm shrugged. "Lost in translation. You know Khadorans when it comes to the more sophisticated linguistics."
"I have a man in the field who might shed some light on this soon," said Rebald.
"Hold a moment. Didn’t Baron Caldwell’s message mention Dusk as well?" asked Leto.
"Caldwell? You mean the chap waiting outside for the last two hours?" said Ebonhart. "On this, of all days."
"Bring him in, then." The queen motioned to a pair of royal guardsmen posted at the great double doors of the chamber, and a moment later, the baron was escorted inside. His brow was damp, and he fidgeted nervously in the presence of the council. After bumbling through the customary formalities, he was invited to take a seat at the end of the table opposite the queen.
"Thank you for your patience, Lord Caldwell," said Leto. "We understand you have something of a certain urgency you wished to bring to our attention. By chance, does it have anything to do with this Dusk business?"
"It does indeed, Lord Raelthorne," replied the baron, pressing both sweaty palms to the table and pushing himself out of his seat. "I have seen what they are and I am here to beseech you to take action at once."

name: Name
body:
"What’s all this  alarm, Caldwell?" said Ebonhart. "What is a Dusk?"
"My Lord Warmaster," the baron said, quivering, "the Dusk are monsters the likes of which you have never seen!"
***

name: Name
body:
Wolfe could feel the destrier beneath him falter again. Its gait had become uneven, and more than once in the last few minutes it had stumbled, just managing to catch itself before taking them both down in the middle of the King’s Highway. The heavy warhorse was as stalwart and resilient as any stallion in the Legion, but these steeds were bred to explode into battle and quickly carry their riders to victory; they lacked the endurance necessary for long distance travel at speed. Even stripped of its barding and barely encumbered by Wolfe’s own arcanely buoyed armor, the mighty horse frothed and gasped as it struggled to keep pace with the strange creatures bearing Hellyth and her Dreadguard.
They called them manticores. It was a name Wolfe associated with a particular class of late Retribution myrmidon, but apparently the Iosan warjacks were named after fearsome beasts that had never been considered anything but myth outside of Ios. Like great predatory felines in their physique but covered in scales like some primordial reptile, the manticores seemed able to run without tiring and, unlike Wolfe’s warhorse whose heavy hooves assaulted the ground beneath him with each stride, their own footfalls barely made a sound.

name: Name
body:
If Wolfe had any appreciation for riding, he might have found himself jealous. But raised the son of a blacksmith, and thus, by default, the reluctant apprentice, Wolfe had no fondness for horses, nor had he ever felt comfortable in the saddle. His gambeson was soaked with sweat, and his armor chaffed in places he was unaccustomed to even being aware of. And the only thought he could hold in his mind was the question of who would expire first: him or the horse?
How long Caldwell’s lead was, Wolfe wasn’t sure. Preparing Vynyshil’s remains to be transported back to the Mistbough had taken time and could not be rushed. The House Kallyss warcaster, Hellyth, Scyir of Nightfall, who had inherited the late councilor’s mission, had insisted on observing the proper rites to protect Vynyshil’s soul as it crossed the mortal veil. Upon completing the necessary rituals, Hellyth had then insisted no time be lost in their remaining journey to Cygnar’s capital city of Caspia.
"Why the sudden urgency?" Wolfe had asked her back at camp.

name: Name
body:
"Time is of the essence," she had said. "I cannot tell you why without compromising the integrity of our purpose."
Wolfe scratched his beard, appearing to consider her words, intentionally stalling just long enough that the eldritch twitched impatiently. "His majesty’s funeral is going to be quite an affair, I’m sure. I’ll regret not being able to honor his passing myself if we don’t arrive in time for the ceremonies. But I’m sure no one will think any less of your gesture if it’s delivered after the formalities. Whatever it might be."
Even though her face was shrouded behind her helm, Hellyth looked away as if eye contact with Wolfe might reveal something better kept secret. "Our condolences for your nation’s loss are genuine. But as you have gleaned, the objective of House Kallyss transcends cordiality."
"You can’t tell me why, but can you tell me about that purpose you mentioned? What exactly is it that you’re looking to achieve?"
Hellyth turned her amber gaze back toward Wolfe and held up a sealed scroll tube. "House Kallyss offers its support to the Kingdom of Cygnar. Without condition."

name: Name
body:
"It’s hard to get past the conditions when you’re talking politics," Wolfe said.
"Politics are exactly what House Kallyss seeks to avoid," she said with finality, stashing the scroll tube in a belt at her side. Wolfe could tell she was impatient to end the discussion and get on with their journey.
"But there’s got to be something motivating you to go through all this trouble." If he hadn’t been worried that something might complicate the plans of House Kallyss, Wolfe would have been amused by the way Hellyth maneuvered through their conversation, dodging his probes, feinting her direction, but never deceiving.
"House Kallyss asks for nothing."
"There’s no such thing as an offer without an ask." Wolfe could feel her amber gaze on his back as he turned back to the assembled lancers awaiting his orders.
It was nearly mid-day by the time they reached the cobbled approach to the northern gate of Caspia. Wolfe signaled for Hellyth and her half-dozen riders to slow down and then put a hand up to let the nine lancers behind him know the same. The rest of his legionnaires as well as the House Kallyss legation had remained behind so that Wolfe could get Hellyth to Caspia as quickly as possible. Marse had accompanied them as well and had been useful in scouting ahead and finding detours around areas that might have resulted in further delays at the sight of Hellyth and her riders. But there were limited routes into Caspia, and there was no getting around going through one of the heavily guarded gates. Marse proceeded ahead to ascertain what they might have to deal with once inside the city walls.

name: Name
body:
Maintaining a walking pace, Wolfe rode next to Hellyth while scanning ahead for potential dangers. "No disrespect intended, but I think it’d be best if you let us approach first."
"Agreed," she replied before rattling off a short burst of commands in Shyrr that prompted her Dreadguard riders to fall in behind the legionnaires.
Several coaches and dozens of foot travelers still awaited entrance through the northern gate. As they approached, Wolfe ordered his lancers into two rows, with two of the legionnaires on either side of him and a row of five behind, creating a wall of armored warriors and warhorses that obscured the eldritch riders behind them. As they drew closer, Wolfe noted a much heavier than normal distribution of guardsmen positioned along the battlements and parapets and an even greater number assembled outside the gates. He knew this wasn’t a standard contingent, even on a day when an abnormally high number of outsiders would be entering the city.
They were preparing for battle.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe and his escort ambled up the causeway until the waiting queue prevented them from proceeding in formation, still some fifty yards from the gates. Travelers stopped their conversations as they spotted the soldiers, and a hush spread across the crowd, becoming so quiet that Wolfe could hear the quiet crackle of his armor’s storm chambers and the hum of the galvanic lances carried by his legionnaires.
"I’ll handle the gatekeepers," Wolfe said to the lancer on his left as he dismounted. "Keep the line tight."
For a moment, Wolfe was grateful just to be on his own two feet. His knees wobbled a bit beneath him as he adjusted to being back on the ground and under his own power, but as he put one foot in front of the other, his steadiness returned. The crowd parted as he walked toward the gate, giving him berth either out of respect for or fear of his station. Though it was an ordinary enough sight for eight-ton steamjacks to walk down a street in any city or town in the Iron Kingdoms, it was a rare and arresting occurrence to see a man clad in storm-powered armor bearing the livery of the nation walking among the commonfolk. But there was no mistaking a warcaster. Men and women like Wolfe were legends in their own time, celebrated by some and reviled by others. But memories of his early life as a stable boy and a blacksmith’s son were never far from his mind, so Wolfe put on his best face and made a deliberate effort to be as cordial and pleasant as possible as he moved among the people that he had sworn his life to protect. And for the most part, they responded in kind until a watchman with a crooked nose broke through the crowd ahead of him.

name: Name
body:
"Good afternoon, Major. We’ve been expecting you." A dozen guardsmen formed up behind the watchman, rifles at high ready.
"Good day to you, Captain." Wolfe paused, glancing up at the sky for a read on the position of the sun, but the heavy clouds obscured it from view. "I was hoping we might be ahead of the noon service."
With a grin, the watch captain plucked a timepiece from his belt, flicked open the cover and stared at it for just a little too long. "Well, then, how’s about we take a look and see, should we?"
And then the noon bell tolled, loud and clear from within the city. Unlike the usual daily bells, however, these were accompanied by blaring horns blowing across the city and along the miles of Caspian walls, hundreds of horns synchronously rendering the heart-rousing national anthem of Cygnar, "For King and Country," ahead of what would be an hour of prayer service held in every chapel around the city.
"Ah, I’m afraid not. Just missed it, I’d say," the watch captain said, clicking his heels and placing his hand over his heart as he lifted his crooked nose toward the sky in reverence of the anthem. The dozen guardsmen behind him shouldered their rifles and followed suit, each a very model of patriotism, inspiring the commonfolk around them to do the same.

name: Name
body: Wolfe massaged his brow, taking a moment to consider what he was up against. Caldwell. "Captain, I am on an urgent diplomatic —" "Shh," the watch captain admonished Wolfe, placing a finger before his lips before returning to his reverent skyward gaze. "I realize the timing—" The watch captain glared at Wolfe. "Major, please. For king and country." "It’s a lovely song, Captain," Wolfe said, taking a step into the man’s space. "But I need to get my people through that gate, and I’ve got no time to lose. Now step aside, please." The watch captain glanced around him as if to make sure no one in authority might spot him speaking during the anthem. He leaned in close. "I’m sorry, Major. The prayer service has begun, and we have strict orders not to let no one in those gates until the observance is over. My hands are tied." The watch captain held up his hands, wrists pressed together as if bound by ropes or shackles. At six-foot-three and clad in powered armor that enabled the wearer to rip a man’s head from his shoulders with ease, Wolfe was used to people stepping aside when he asked them to. And any soldier in the Cygnaran military wouldn’t have hesitated at the request. But the city watchmen were not under the purview of the military, and Wolfe’s rank had no jurisdiction or influence over their agency.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe swallowed and considered his diplomatic options. "Captain, I beseech you. I must present this legation as quickly as possible."
The captain nodded. "Of course, Major. I’ll put you at the front of the queue and get you in ahead of everyone else…soon as the service ends."
It was clear to Wolfe the watch captain was enjoying his imposition too much. He longed for his warjacks at his side. City watch or anyone else, no one stood up to a warjack because warjacks didn’t reason or worry about repercussions. But even as he contemplated adopting a more aggressive, warjack-like approach to the standoff, the watch captain suddenly recoiled in fear. The guardsmen behind him snapped out of their anthem reverie and drew their rifles on Wolfe.
Then Wolfe felt chitinous scales brush across his left arm and realized the rifles weren’t being aimed at him. Hellyth pushed forward while atop the manticore she had ridden to the city. It was precisely the moment Wolfe had hoped to avoid.
"We must not delay, Major Wolfe," she rasped; he could see the captain and those behind him react to the unnatural sound of her voice. "Seconds are precious."

name: Name
body: "Morrow help us," the watch captain sputtered, pointing a quivering finger at Hellyth as he backed away through the line of guardsmen. "It’s even more horrible than described." Wolfe held up his hands. "Now let’s just take a moment here—" "We have no more moments," Hellyth said, cutting him off. Wolfe knew the guardsmen were mere seconds from someone doing something stupid. The men were nervous; the watch captain was a jaded fool. And Hellyth didn’t know how to read humans. "Hellyth—Scyir—you’ve got to give me something to work with," Wolfe pleaded. "These men are just doing their job. But I’m sure they’ll be reasonable if we can explain the urgency." Desperation made it harder for Hellyth to speak, the labor of forcing air in and out of lungs that no longer worked on their own, too much to deal with. "Explanation," she wheezed, "defiles…our purpose." Wolfe clocked the watch captain raising a brass whistle as he attempted to melt behind the guards. He could hear the watchman say, "If that beast takes another step forward, shoot it and the rider."

name: Name
body:
Nervous murmurs and frightened gasps rippled through the crowded avenue around them.
"Captain, I’m asking you, please," Wolfe said, reaching out an open palm as the captain slinked backward. "We don’t want any of these people to get hurt."
"Major Wolfe," Hellyth whispered, "do I have your trust?"
Wolfe’s attention was torn between the unpredictable captain, the guardsmen with their quivering trigger fingers, and Hellyth. "I trust your intentions, Scyir. I do. But I need you to follow my lead. One false move out here, and the men atop that wall will drop the portcullis, and we won’t make it into the city before tomorrow morning."
But it was too late. The watch captain put the whistle to his lips and blew.
It was a shrill, piercing shriek that caused an instant commotion along the battlements. In that same instant, Hellyth hissed what sounded like a vile curse in Shyrr and yanked back the reins on her mount. The creature reared up and roared ferociously, raking at the air with its claws. A shot rang out, then an entire fusillade as the guards opened fire on the manticore. Many of the bullets glanced harmlessly off its indigo scales while other ripped bloody wounds in its underside.

name: Name
body:
Glowing disks of amber runes exploded from Hellyth’s palms, spinning and expanding as they flew from her hands to encircle the guardsmen before dissolving into a shadowy shroud that seemed to bind them in place even as they struggled to retreat. On her command, the Dreadguard manticore riders bounded past the immobilized guardsmen and began to clear a path through the crowded avenue. The travelers scattered in the face of the snarling manticores and the terrifying eldritch war-maidens atop them.
"Now, Major! To the gate!" Hellyth shouted hoarsely. "Trust me!"
Spurring her manticore forward, Hellyth vaulted over the guardsmen just as another volley of shots rang out.
"I wasn’t ready for this," Wolfe growled under his breath as he dashed for his horse and clambered gracelessly into the saddle. He turned to his lancers. "You heard the lady! Get in that gate!"
As Hellyth made her way up the avenue, the watch captain came after her, blasting his whistle. Wolfe wished he were a better rider and could have snatched it out of watchman’s hands as he rode by, but it was all he could do to stay atop the horse as it galloped over the cobblestones, and he was afraid he’d accidentally trample the man to death if he made such an attempt.

name: Name
body:
Before Hellyth could close half the distance to the gate, however, there was a crack like the splintering of a tree followed by an earth-shaking crash: the gate’s massive portcullis smashed into the ground, barricading the full height of the hundred-foot-high entry arch with iron bars as thick as a man’s leg.
Wolfe’s heart sank. It would take a full day to reset the massive portcullis and raise it after an emergency lockdown. Such an extreme measure of dropping the portcullis was rarely taken, and Wolfe knew that Caldwell must have worked hard, or at least paid handsomely, to prime the watch for such a reaction.
The causeway burst into chaos. Travelers fled from the gates as the manticores yowled at the blocked entrance. Wolfe slowed the lancers to avoid running over civilians and guardsmen alike, but he couldn’t prevent those on foot from trampling each other. And then the gunfire erupted from the walls. Thanks to the panicked whistles of the watch captain, the alleged attack the guards had been braced for had come Wolfe knew how bad it must look from the battlements above as the gates were rushed by a fearsome and unfamiliar enemy, pursued by Storm Legion cavalry straight to the sealed arch of the northern gate.

name: Name
body:
Scores of watchmen assembled along the terraced ramparts, sighting down their long rifles at Hellyth and her six riders. Not even a warjack could survive the withering fire of so many long gunners, but Hellyth refused to retreat.
Wolfe stood up in his stirrups, waving his arms and bellowing at the top of his lungs. "Hold fire!" But even his thunderous voice was drowned out by the uproar.
A hail of rifle bullets rained down upon the Dreadguard, yet Hellyth stood still before the gate and spread her arms out wide, conjuring an arcane force that appeared to emanate from her in shadowy, circular waves. It was as if the image in front of Wolfe was a reflection in a dark lake shattered by a single pebble. The ripples spread out, colliding with each of Hellyth’s Dreadguard, which then became their own source of the dark waves. This disrupted their visibility to the guardsmen and seemed to strengthen the Dreadguards’ resilience against what few shots still found their mark. The enchantment protected the riders and their mounts, at least for the moment.

name: Name
body:
But the city watch quickly realized the source of the ward and concentrated their fire on Hellyth alone. Wolfe could tell she was directing her full focus into powering the forcefield generated by her armor—arcantrik vents and nodes in her carapace bloomed with sorcerous fire. Even as he closed the last few steps to her, though, he saw her shoulder jerk as a shot punched through.
Then another and another.
Hellyth’s body and her mount were riddled by the endless barrage of gunfire until the fiery channels and nodes of her armor dimmed and her beast crumpled beneath her. They both collapsed into a bloody heap on the ground.
Wolfe pushed his horse into the line of fire, rearing up to distract the gunners and foil their aim.
"Form up on me!" he roared to his lancers as he leaped from his horse to shield her body with his own. One by one, the armored legionnaires did the same, dropping their lances and raising their shields as they circled around their leader, creating a dome of blue and gold above him.

name: Name
body:
Would they fire on their own? Wolfe wondered. Taking no chances, he conjured a pair of spells, encircling his soldiers with luminous blue runes that created a shimmering barrier around them and encased their armor in a radiant glow.
Kneeling down beneath the protective canopy, he carefully scooped Hellyth up and leaned her against the fallen manticore. Black ichor oozed from a dozen wounds; her limbs were limp; and Wolfe could feel the chill of her essence draining from her. Gently, he removed her helmet. Blood ran from her eyes like two black inkwells that had run over onto her ashen white face.
Yet she lived.
She sputtered painfully, struggling to make her words audible. "I can…get you through…the gate."
Wolfe shook his head. Did it matter now? "How?"
"Take…this." She clutched the scroll tube still, raising it slightly. "Tell your people…it is…our pledge."
"Hellyth—" Wolfe could feel her spirit slipping from her body.
"Trust…us," she whispered, her eyes closing. Ancient glowing runes ignited at her fingertips, spiraling around Wolfe. "Go…tell them."

name: Name
body: He could feel her sorcery at work as the world around him appeared increasingly translucent and ghostly, as if he could walk right through his Legionnaires next to him and the iron bars beyond them. "Tell them yourself." Wolfe pulled off her gauntlets and placed her hands on either side of his face, her flesh contacting his. Hellyth’s eyes snapped open. Like completing an electric circuit, he could feel the eldritch’s icy essence flowing through him, burrowing into his very being. "No," she hissed, aghast, but she could not pull his hands away. Her fingers pressed into his flesh. "Trust me," Wolfe said, rising to his feet with Hellyth in his arms. "On me!" he called out to the legionnaires, who kept their shields raised around him as he marched toward the gate. Hellyth drank in Wolfe’s life force. It was as if a void had opened within his mind, his vital energy being sucked from him. The void spread to his chest and through his limbs, consuming everything he could sense and feel and leaving behind an unfathomable emptiness. His knees quivered and he stumbled mere paces from the arch as his strength vanished. In a fog, he could hear the watch captain’s whistle then the distant plink of bullets ricocheting off his soldiers’ shields. He could no longer feel his feet upon the ground or the weight of Hellyth in his arms. All sensation had been replaced with a dreadful hollowness as if in moments, he might simply cease to exist. But Hellyth’s amber rune circles still orbited him, and he could see the translucent bars of the massive iron portcullis ahead. The muffled sound of his legionnaires’ confused voices drifted through what was left of his consciousness, trying to pull him back to reality. But without slowing, Wolfe walked straight into the bars with Hellyth in his arms, passing through solid iron like a phantom before his mind dissolved to black.

name: Name
body:
How much time had passed he could not tell, but the icy grip on his vital essence released, and the void inside him receded, replaced by a numbness that gave way to an intense heat, then searing pain as the force that gave Wolfe life flowed back into every crevasse of his being. And then his mind exploded with a hellish vision of carnage and destruction, of cities burning and endless waves of death wrought at the hands of a barbaric horde, clad in armor adorned with howling faces.
He staggered and pitched forward but a firm hand caught his arm and held him steady. When he was able to lift his head, he saw Hellyth standing before him. Her wounds had closed; her face was rejuvenated. And the world around him was solid once more.
Wolfe winced as the pain subsided. "What was that I saw?"
Hellyth’s expression was even more grim than usual. "A possible future. I’m sorry, it is difficult to contain one’s mind during communion."
"This is what you hope to stop?" Wolfe asked. "The Orgoth."
Hellyth nodded. "They have already returned."

name: Name
body:
Inside the gate, Marse had arrived with a dozen legionnaires, who quickly formed a defensive circle around Wolfe and Hellyth. The city watch inside the gate had stepped aside, looking sheepish in the presence of the much more heavily armed soldiers. And a trio of sharp shooters were ensuring that the captain of the watch refrained from another whistle fit. Equally significant, Hellyth’s Dreadguard had found shelter under the arch of the great entrance. Despite the purview of the city watch to uphold the law within the city, Wolfe enjoyed the home turf advantage now that he was inside the walls where the Storm Legion was garrisoned.
***

name: Name
body:
Four royal guardsmen in blue tabards and gold helms escorted Wolfe, Marse, Hellyth, and a pair of legionnaires to the chamber of the Inner Council. Outside the chamber, a second pair of guards requested that they turn over all weapons. Hellyth only reluctantly complied after Wolfe assured her that it was a standard practice, though one more often reserved for potentially hazardous meetings. He suspected the council had been advised before they arrived of some potential danger Hellyth—and perhaps even Wolfe —might present.
They were admitted within and announced to the queen and the chancellors. But tension in the room was high, and a half-dozen royal guards were posted around the table with another half-dozen flanking the queen. Meanwhile, the four guards who had escorted them in took positions around a sideboard in one corner where Hellyth’s pistols had been placed next to Wolfe’s weapons and the stormthrower lightning blades belonging to the legionnaires. It was a level of security Wolfe had not seen in all his years presenting at council meetings inside the palace; he was sure it had been inspired by the infectious paranoia of Baron Caldwell. As such, he took great satisfaction in seeing the color run out of the man’s face the instant Caldwell laid eyes on them.

name: Name
body:
The baron scrambled out of his seat as Wolfe and Hellyth approached the table. "Your Majesty, my lords. It is not safe to be in here with this demon."
Wolfe held out his empty hands. "Easy now, Lord Caldwell. We’ve handed over our weapons."
"This one can kill with a touch! All her kind can." Caldwell jabbed his finger toward Hellyth. "And she has put a hex on the major. He’s blind to her devilry, and you all know what he’s capable of, even unarmed."
All eyes were on Hellyth, and the expressions around the table ranged from unfriendly to frightened except for the queen, who appeared more curious than concerned.
"I’ve known Major Wolfe for many years," Leto said. "He seems as sound of mind as he’s always been." The High Chancellor squinted in Wolfe’s direction. "Are you under a spell, Major?"
"No, my lord," Wolfe sighed.
"With all due respect, Lord Raelthorne," Rebald said quietly for the benefit of those around the table only, "he likely wouldn’t tell you if he was."
"I can assure you, sir," Marse said, addressing his commanding officer, "Major Wolfe has not been compromised. The baron has misinterpreted what he’s seen. Our House Kallyss friends are more than a wee bit different, I’ll be the first to admit, maybe even a little cold to the touch, but they’re even more just like you and me…you know, save for the dead bit."

name: Name
body:
Wolfe squeezed Marse’s arm gently, hoping to rein in his runaway mouth. "Your Majesty. My lords," Wolfe said. "With respect to the unfortunate timing of events, the House Kallyss delegation has traveled far to request this audience with the queen. I strongly recommend we proceed with haste."
"Interruptions appear to be the fashion of the day," the warmaster said impatiently. "You know, it’s called the ‘Inner Council’ because it’s typically by invitation only. This isn’t the venue for receiving diplomats or entertaining random concerns. If it weren’t for your admirable record, Major, you wouldn’t have been let through those doors, much less with…" He trailed off, seeming unable to find the appropriate words, and instead resorted to a somewhat dismissive gesture in Hellyth’s direction.
"We have a matter of national security to discuss, and a king to lay to rest," Queen Marjorie spoke up. "If you believe your business should take precedence, then let’s have it."
"Thank you, your Majesty. I believe we cannot afford another moment’s delay," Wolfe said then stepped back to allow Hellyth to address the council.

name: Name
body:
Though some of the more severe qualities of her eldritch transformation were softened by the recent communion, to those gazing upon Hellyth’s face for the first time, she was a chilling sight, deathly pale with waxy flesh stretched tight across her gaunt features. But if the queen felt any sense of shock or disgust or alarm, she betrayed no sign of it. The same could not be said for everyone at the table.
"Thank you...Your Majesty," Hellyth said, her voice hoarse and hollow. "I am Hellyth, Scyir of Nightfall, Arms Master…" She paused, her head twitching slightly as she seemed to recalibrate her introduction. "…and  Seeker of the late Consulate Court, council to House Kallyss, Preeminent Chamber of the High Convocation of the Empire of the Eternal Dusk."
From her waistbelt, she produced the scroll tube. "We seek an alliance."
A guard stepped forward and accepted the scroll tube, unsheathing the contents and offering them to Queen Marjorie. The queen unfurled a single piece of exquisite parchment, its edges kissed with gold leaf. Written upon it in carefully penned Cygnaran were but a few lines declaring the proposal of a mutually beneficial agreement between House Kallyss and Cygnar to ensure the ongoing safety and prosperity of their respective nations. The queen was confounded. "An alliance? Are these your terms? It doesn’t say anything.

name: Name
body:
The queen’s eyes darted from the parchment to Hellyth to Wolfe and then around the table, as if she were missing the punchline of a joke that everyone else was in on.
"There are no terms. It just says that you wish an alliance." Her brow creased as she handed the parchment to Leto. "Which is as you stated. But…what do you want?"
"House Kallyss asks for nothing," Hellyth said.
"But that’s not how these things work," interjected Ebonhart. "An alliance must be negotiated. You offer something and tell us what you want. We offer something and ask for what we want. We go back and forth and eventually agree on terms. But it takes time. We cannot agree to an alliance with a nation we know nothing about. There’s a process. It hasn't been too long since your nation harbored an army of extremists who were happy to kill our citizens, you know. We haven’t heard from Ios in decades."
"Ios is no more. Ios had…no allies," Hellyth said. Despite the levelness of her voice, Wolfe had spent enough time around the Scyir that he thought he detected the pangs of regret. "Now, there is the Dusk. House Kallyss, of the Empire of the Eternal Dusk, will not go unseen when an ally is in need."

name: Name
body:
"I don’t understand," Marjorie said, looking at Wolfe. "What is it they want?"
Wolfe was slow to choose his answer. "Acceptance."
Hellyth turned her gaze toward him, but whether she agreed or felt he was in error, she said nothing.
"Acceptance of what, Major? This is no time to be obscure," Marjorie said.
Wolfe nodded. "I understand. Acceptance of their existence. Acceptance of their differences. Acceptance of who and what they are."
"Without concern for what they have to offer," Leto interjected. He was nodding as well.
"Exactly," Wolfe said. "You might be willing to overlook something objectionable in someone you felt had a great deal to offer. But they’re not looking for a short-term gain, and I think House Kallyss doesn’t want to be courted out of convenience, either."
Leto seemed intrigued, and even at his age his mind was as sharp as ever. "They seek a pure alliance free of motive, free of politics, which all eventually…"
"Decay," Hellyth said, returning her attention to the queen.
Marjorie looked directly into the Scyir’s eyes. "It’s unheard of. We will need time to consider this."

name: Name
body:
"There is no more time, your Majesty," Hellyth said, taking a step forward, prompting the guards around the queen to ready their halberds. "Your nation is in peril. All of your Iron Kingdoms are, as is the Empire of Eternal Dusk. Even now, Khador bleeds. Your destroyer has returned."
Sparholm shook his head, incredulous. "Khador bleeds? Is this that Orgoth nonsense again?"
"It’s a trick is what it is," Caldwell spoke up, looking increasingly more agitated as he paced along the wall as far from Hellyth as he could get.
"You know of their return, then?" Wolfe said to the chancellors.
"We know someone’s claiming the Orgoth are back," said Ebonhart, "But we have no evidence, just a suspicious wire and the wild talk of this…what was it again? Scyir of Nightfall?"
"I believe it all to be true, Lord Ebonhart," Wolfe said.
"Your earnestness is not taken for granted, Major," said the queen, "But have you actually seen them?"
"Not exactly." Wolfe looked at Hellyth. "You must show her."
"Show me what?" Marjorie asked uneasily.

name: Name
body:
"A vision," Wolfe said, nodding to Hellyth, who appeared as apprehensive as the queen at Wolfe’s cryptic suggestion.
"May I, your Majesty?" Hellyth said, removing her glove while slowly stepping forward.
At this, Caldwell came unhinged. "No, Your Majesty! Her touch is death!"
The guardsmen stepped forward to block Hellyth’s approach.
"I assure you, the Scyir is of no danger," Wolfe said.
"It’s how they feed," Caldwell shouted. "Don’t let her near you, any of you!"
Anxious murmurs spread among the chancellors. The queen raised one palm in front of her, hesitating. "Perhaps we should not…"
But Caldwell had taken matters into his own hands. With all eyes on Hellyth, the baron slipped behind the guardsmen watching over the weapons and hoisted one of the heavy stormthrowers, pulling the lever that opened the blades to reveal a lightning coil within.
"Leave her alone, demon!" Caldwell cried, leveling the weapon. When he pulled the trigger on the stormthrower, it unleashed a crackling tendril of lightning that scorched the stone floor as it snaked toward Hellyth.

name: Name
body:
Wolfe’s eyes flashed with arcane energy. He leaped forward to intercept the stream of electricity with his own body, the insulation of his armor crafted to protect him from the effects of the Legion’s weapons. Hellyth was unscathed, but the raging stormthrower was more than the baron could handle. In his effort to correct his aim, Caldwell lost control of the weapon, arcing the tendril of lightning around the chamber and over the heads of the chancellors, scoring black gouges in the stone, igniting tapestries on the walls, and exploding hanging gas lamps that illuminated the room.
As the bolt carved a fissure across the back wall of the chamber it arced to the chains suspending the mighty Cygnaran crest suspended behind the queen, rupturing the fasteners that held it in place. The crest crashed thunderously to the floor behind the queen and toppled forward. Hunkered low in her chair, she could not possibly escape in time.
But glowing runes burst into spirals around Hellyth as she rushed forward, her ghostly form passing directly through the guardsmen who had sought to block her path. Seizing the queen’s wrist, she pulled her toward her, just as the massive golden Cygnus fell forward, smashing the end of the great council table to splinters.

name: Name
body:
And in the moment the Scyir’s flesh touched her own, Queen Marjorie’s mind exploded into a nightmare.
***

name: Name
body:
She was surrounded by an impossible hellscape. The walls of Caspia were engulfed in flames, two-hundred-foot-high infernos that cracked and crumbled the blackened stone. The streets were littered with corpses of Cygnaran soldiers and civilians, piled like fallen timbers against the burning buildings. Howling barbarians with blazing weapons mercilessly butchered terror-stricken Caspians fleeing from the carnage. Devastating machines in the shape of abominable creatures clawed at the palace gates of Castle Raelthorne until they were torn from their hinges and a towering, helmed figure, the Destroyer, clad in armor adorned with ghastly faces, strode through. In one hand, she carried a barbed spear and in the other, she dragged the bound body of an unmistakably divine being whose radiance was fading as quickly as the river of blood that flowed out of his countless wounds.
Halting before the palace doors, the Destroyer cast the body face down at her feet and then drove the spear through his back before lifting him skyward and thrusting the shaft of the spear into the ground.

name: Name
body:
As the light of the divine being died, cracks formed at the base of the palace, spreading upward like vines until they reached the highest spires of the castle. And then, stone by stone, level by level, the palace crumbled to the ground.
Caspia, the only city that had survived the original Orgoth occupation a half-millennium past, was reduced to smoldering rubble.
***

name: Name
body:
Wolfe knelt over the queen. Her eyes remained closed.
He had inserted himself between the guards and Hellyth to ensure the communion between the Scyir and his queen was undisturbed. Fortunately, the sequence of events had moved so quickly and unexpectedly that Queen Marjorie was safe before anyone could react, and Hellyth was able to leave her in the care of Wolfe as quickly as she was rescued from the falling crest.
By the time Marjorie opened her eyes, Caldwell was being detained by a pair of royal guardsmen and had lost his enthusiasm for speaking out.
A physician was called while Wolfe and Sparholm helped Marjorie into a chair. She appeared uninjured and fully capable, but she trembled as if in shock. As soon as she took her seat, she covered her face with her hands and wept.
No one spoke, not even the gallery of chancellors who rarely had a moment of silence between them. After several minutes, Marjorie dried her eyes, rose, and walked to stand before Hellyth.
"How can we prevent this horror from coming to pass?" she asked, her voice quiet and uneven.

name: Name
body:
"We do not know that we can," replied Hellyth, "But we know how we will not. Separate. Alone. Helpless."
"Then we shall do the one thing these Orgoth would never expect," Marjorie said, taking Hellyth’s hands in her own. "Let us  stand together."

name: Dead on Arrival\nPart 4 - Chapter 1 Dead on Arrival: Part 4
